title: Idiopathic intracranial hypertension: impaired CSF resorption (venous hypertension)
vignette: A 19-year-old woman with obesity comes to the office due to bifrontal headaches and early-morning nausea and vomiting for 4 weeks. She appears alert and is cooperative. Blood pressure is 114/78 mm Hg and pulse is 80/min. BMI is 31 kg/m2. Funduscopy shows bilateral papilledema. Visual acuity is 20/20 bilaterally. Neurologic examination shows no abnormalities. CT scan of the head reveals no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely explanation for this patient's symptoms?

clues.note: A young, obese woman of childbearing age is the classic demographic for idiopathic intracranial hypertension (pseudotumor cerebri).

clues.text: bifrontal headaches and early-morning nausea and vomiting
clues.note: Headache with nausea/vomiting worse in the morning (recumbency) is typical of increased intracranial pressure.
Bilateral papilledema is the objective sign of increased intracranial pressure - central to the diagnosis of idiopathic intracranial hypertension.

clues.text: CT scan of the head reveals no abnormalities
clues.note: Increased ICP with a NORMAL CT (no mass, no hydrocephalus) is characteristic of idiopathic intracranial hypertension.

whatMatters: Young obese woman + headache + papilledema + NORMAL CT (no mass/hydrocephalus) = IDIOPATHIC INTRACRANIAL HYPERTENSION (pseudotumor cerebri). The elevated ICP results from DECREASED CSF RESORPTION, thought to be due to elevated CEREBRAL VENOUS pressure (impairing arachnoid granulation drainage). Answer C.
strategy: Recognize idiopathic intracranial hypertension (elevated ICP, papilledema, normal imaging in an obese young woman) and reason about CSF dynamics: ICP rises from reduced RESORPTION (venous hypertension impairing arachnoid granulations), not overproduction. Reject increased CSF production (rare choroid plexus papilloma, would show a mass/ventriculomegaly), aqueductal stenosis (obstructive hydrocephalus - ventriculomegaly on CT), astrocyte (cytotoxic) swelling (cerebral edema visible on CT), and neurodegeneration (atrophy, normal/low ICP).

eliminations.label: Aqueductal stenosis - obstructive hydrocephalus (ventriculomegaly)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: narrowing of the cerebral aqueduct blocking CSF flow from the third to fourth ventricle. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it causes obstructive hydrocephalus with DILATED lateral/third ventricles on CT; this patient's CT is normal. ✅ Correct if: enlarged ventricles from aqueductal obstruction.

eliminations.label: Astrocyte swelling - cytotoxic cerebral edema (visible on CT)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: cytotoxic cerebral edema (astrocyte swelling) raising ICP. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: edema is usually APPARENT on CT (effaced sulci, poor gray-white differentiation); here the CT is normal. ✅ Correct if: CT showing cerebral edema.

eliminations.label: Increased CSF production - choroid plexus papilloma (mass/ventriculomegaly)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: overproduction of CSF, classically by a choroid plexus papilloma. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: that would show an intraventricular mass and ventriculomegaly on imaging; idiopathic intracranial hypertension is a RESORPTION problem with normal imaging. ✅ Correct if: an intraventricular mass causing ventriculomegaly.

eliminations.label: Neurodegeneration - atrophy, not raised ICP
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: neuronal loss/atrophy (e.g., Alzheimer). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it decreases brain volume (hydrocephalus ex vacuo) with normal/low ICP, not papilledema/elevated ICP. ✅ Correct if: dementia with cerebral atrophy.

reasoning: Obese young woman + headache + papilledema + NORMAL CT = idiopathic intracranial hypertension
Elevated ICP here reflects impaired CSF RESORPTION, not overproduction or obstruction
The impaired resorption is attributed to elevated cerebral VENOUS pressure (poor arachnoid-granulation drainage)
mechanism: Idiopathic intracranial hypertension (pseudotumor cerebri) is elevated intracranial pressure WITHOUT a mass lesion, hydrocephalus, or other structural cause, occurring most often in obese women of reproductive age. Cerebrospinal fluid is produced by the choroid plexus, circulates through the ventricular system, and is normally reabsorbed by the ARACHNOID GRANULATIONS into the cerebral venous sinuses. In idiopathic intracranial hypertension, the problem is DECREASED CSF RESORPTION, thought to result from elevated CEREBRAL VENOUS pressure (venous hypertension/sinus stenosis) that reduces the pressure gradient for CSF drainage across the arachnoid granulations; the accumulating CSF raises ICP. Clinically: headache (worse recumbent/on waking), nausea/vomiting, papilledema, and sometimes transient visual obscurations or a sixth-nerve palsy - with NORMAL neuroimaging and normal CSF composition (but elevated opening pressure). Untreated, it threatens vision. Management includes weight loss, acetazolamide (reduces CSF production), and, if vision is threatened, CSF shunting or optic nerve sheath fenestration. The distractors involve obstruction (aqueductal stenosis), edema (astrocyte swelling), overproduction (choroid plexus papilloma), or atrophy (neurodegeneration) - none fits raised ICP with a normal CT.

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid Neuro > idiopathic intracranial hypertension: obese young women, headache + papilledema, normal imaging, ↑opening pressure; impaired CSF resorption (venous hypertension); treat weight loss + acetazolamide.

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: Raised ICP with normal CT in an obese young woman = idiopathic intracranial hypertension from decreased CSF resorption (venous hypertension).

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on idiopathic intracranial hypertension/pseudotumor cerebri, papilledema, arachnoid granulations, or CSF resorption? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: Aqueductal stenosis (ventriculomegaly), astrocyte swelling (edema on CT), CSF overproduction (papilloma/mass), neurodegeneration (atrophy) all show imaging changes or wrong physiology.

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: idiopathic intracranial hypertension = ↓CSF resorption (cerebral venous hypertension); obese young women; treat weight loss + acetazolamide.

Neuro > headache, papilledema, transient visual obscurations, CN VI palsy.

memoryHook: Pseudotumor = pressure with a clean scan: the CSF drain (arachnoid granulations) is backed up by high venous pressure, so fluid pools and the optic disc swells.
